body.statement: There are constants \(c,C\) and events \(\mathcal E_n\) with \(\inf_{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa}P(\mathcal E_n)\geq1-Cn^{-3}\) such that, simultaneously for \(h\in H_n\) and \(u\in U_n\) satisfying \(n_1u\geq C\log(en)\), \[J_P(h,u)\leq\widehat J(h,c\{u+\log(en)/n_1\})\leq C J_P(h/8,C\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}).\] On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)\) for every \(x,h\), and the bounds are within constant factors when \(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\). For every \(h\in H_n\), the source-labeled lexicographic sorting, duplicate removal, and midpoint map defining \(C_1(h)\) and \(G_1(h)\) are Borel functions of \((X_i)_{i\in I_1}\); the finite maximum defining \(\widehat J(h,u)\) is therefore Borel for every \(u\in U_n\). The confidence calibration, zero-count event, and \(h_0\)-fallback event together contribute at most \(C(L+\sigma)\log^2(en)/n\) to expected supremum risk and introduce no leading global \(\log n\) factor on \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\).
body.justification: This proof-critical component prevents both an implicit selector and a hidden global logarithm in Theorem 1.
body.gap: Design-adaptive regression does not supply the measurable severity-layer packing comparison needed for this boundary oracle theorem; the lemma is supporting rather than a second headline claim.
body.consumer: It certifies that the implementable penalty distinguishes localized support holes from pervasive scarcity without measurability gaps.
